result.angle: Concept-word grep (English nouns/verbs and their stems, comments and docstrings included) across src/, supabase/ and the in-tree docs of the build slot (claude/composite-r4 @ f73bdbf16), then opening every hit and asking whether the code DOES the thing — deliberately avoiding the first pass's wave labels, flag names and module names. The consist (laneCONSIST-930) was checked for the same terms and is identical on every point below.

rows.target: Transitive relay + passage predicate (LG-0/LG-1; §125.1) — relay explicit; passage predicate allied-or-beneficial, widened to traders
rows.evidence: RELAY IS REAL, AND MULTI-HOP. src/domain/spatial/distanceRead.js:~790-806 `augmentedAdjacency()` folds the frozen teleport edge set into the land gate graph via `linkMin`, and `shortestPath()` (:~830-870) runs a deterministic Dijkstra over it — so A→circle→circle→B relays transitively with no special-casing. STILL ENDPOINT-GATED: `routingAdjacency(digest,a,b)` at distanceRead.js:~816-822 returns the augmented graph only when `isTeleportNode(digest,a) || isTeleportNode(digest,b)`, so a non-holder cannot relay THROUGH a bloc it does not touch. NO WILLINGNESS PREDICATE ANYWHERE. src/domain/spatial/teleportEdges.js:21-26 names it in prose only — 'The network is a CLIQUE OF THE WILLING … The WILLINGNESS (non-hostile diplomacy) is a READ-TIME property … the diplomatic gate composes through the existing danger/relationship seams' — and then `buildTeleportEdgeSet` (:193-213) emits the full unconditional clique with `{between, cost, capacity}` and nothing else; the only gates in the module are institutional (`hasTeleportInstitution` :136) and magical (`magicFunctionsAt` :124). Grepping the whole of src/domain/spatial for hostile/non-hostile/allied/ally/beneficial returns exactly ONE line — that same docblock at teleportEdges.js:22. No caller re-filters the edge set by relationship before routing.
rows.searched: willingness, willing, hostile, non-hostile, allied, ally, beneficial, passage, relay, transitive, clique of the willing, read-time property, diplomatic gate — all across src/domain/spatial, src/domain/worldPulse, supabase/

rows.target: Trade use of the circles — allies pass free / trading partners pay a toll / wartime military use PREEMPTS trade on limited capacity (§125.1 + §125a)
rows.evidence: No toll, no exemption, no preemption and no capacity throttle touches a teleport edge. teleportEdges.js:40-44 states the position in its own words: 'CAPACITY — TELEPORT_EDGE_CAPACITY, a LOW ceiling … v1 routing reads COST, not capacity (no throttle yet — the abstraction, mirroring M8 sea-lane v1); recorded on each edge for the bounded-trade + node-starvation flow work', and :74-75 repeats it at the constant. `TELEPORT_EDGE_CAPACITY = 2` is written onto every edge at :203 and read by nobody. Greps for preempt/preemption/priority of use/wartime use return zero hits in src/ and supabase/. THE TWO NEAR-MISSES, both refuted: (1) the entrepôt toll — src/domain/spatial/entrepots.js:13-17 and src/domain/spatial/embattlement.js:156 `tollRateOf(worldState,id)` summed over intermediaries at embattlement.js:338/:355 — is a FLAT per-through-LAND-NODE surcharge with no payer dimension at all (no ally, partner or wartime branch), and it never sees a teleport hop. (2) the treaty toll-exemption family — src/domain/worldPulse/peaceTermsCatalog.js:287 `toll_exemption: … executor: 'seam'`, where :93 defines 'seam' as "typed-now, fed later" and :146 as 'a typed registration seam (executor unlanded)'. Its only live consumer is display: src/domain/institutions/institutionTable.js:479-481 filters treatyTerms for /toll/ ∧ /exempt/ and renders the string `toll exemption on <route>`; no arithmetic anywhere reduces a toll because of it.
rows.searched: toll, passage fee, circle fee, preempt, preemption, priority of use, wartime use, allies pass free, exemption, exempt, throttle, capacity ceiling, tollRateOf, toll_exemption

rows.target: Airships (LG-3/LG-4) — one origin port, reduced travel time, air battles
rows.evidence: CARGO CHANNEL IS REAL (confirming the first pass): src/data/foodImportRates.js:18-22 sets `airship: 0.3 / airshipBesieged: 0.15`; src/generators/foodGenerator.js:137-146 distinguishes the two magic channels explicitly ('Circles and airships are NOT interchangeable: a teleportation circle is point-to-point and a blockade cannot touch it; an airship must fly over'), :279-292 picks `airshipBesieged` under siege, :445-446 stamps `magicTradeChannel: 'teleport'|'airship'`; the tick-time twin is src/domain/worldPulse/foodStockpile.js:311-316 (`_bypassShare` from `resolveBlockadeBypassChannel`) inside the pulse. Generation will even FORCE the institution: src/generators/isolationGenerator.js:58-93 prefers an airship dock at magicPriority ≥ 80 ∧ metropolis and otherwise a circle, pushing it with `forcedByIsolation: true`. TRAVEL MODE STILL ABSENT. The digest's air slot is pinned dead: src/domain/spatial/spatialDigest.js:193 `return { airField: null, seaLanes: …, seasonalOverlay: …, teleportEdges: … }` — `airField` is a hard `null` literal with no builder, and :38/:186 are the only other mentions in the tree. Greps for 'by air', 'aerial' (only institution descriptions and a service label), overflight, flight/flying (only in-flight render latches and a flying buttress), 'air battle' and 'reduced time' find nothing that moves a traveller. `travelMode` exists but is a single-valued rules key: src/domain/worldPulse/simulationRules.js:55 `travelMode: 'instant'`, and :1358 says outright 'spatialMode/travelMode: single meaningful value today'. So there is no air hop, no air hop-time, and no air combat.

rows.target: Unified vessel pool (LG-2; L-LG-2) — a fleet per settlement, trade-or-war, unavailable until return
rows.evidence: THE 'UNAVAILABLE UNTIL RETURN' ARM IS BUILT, as a per-port exclusivity lock the first pass's module-name search could not see. src/domain/worldPulse/realmVerbExecution.js:527-528 — `const records = asObject(getSpatialLedger(state,'navalTransit')); if (records[ownerId]) return refused(refuse('convoy_refused','the fleet is already at sea'));` — and the identical guard for blockades at :553-554 (`refuse('blockade_refused','the fleet is already at sea')`). The organic path enforces the same rule: src/domain/worldPulse/navalKernel.js:332 `if (records[armyId]) continue; // this navy already has a live operation`. The lock releases on RETURN, not on a timer: navalKernel.js:304-317 stands a convoy down on arrival (`if (stepped.position01 >= 1)`) or on recall, and :319-326 lifts a blockade when the pair stops being hostile — dropping the record and freeing the port to act again. The ledger key is per-port-settlement (`ownerId` is gated `isPort` at realmVerbExecution.js:522/:551). WHAT IS STILL MISSING: no fleet SIZE or count anywhere (0 hits for vesselPool, shipPool, fleetSize, flotilla, hulls-as-a-count, tonnage, 'ships available'); strength is re-derived every tick and never persisted (src/domain/spatial/navalLayer.js:18-26 'one navy per port settlement, capability DERIVED, NEVER PERSISTED'); and the lock is BINARY — one operation, not a pool drawn down. Above all there is no TRADE-OR-WAR contention: nothing on the trade side (commodityFlow, supplyShipments, entrepots) reads or writes `navalTransit`, so a port's merchant traffic never competes with its war fleet for bottoms. The only sea-side scarcity that exists is per-LANE, not per-fleet: navalLayer.js:~317/:~332 `seaLaneCapacityOf` + `convoyCapacityAvailable` defer a convoy when a lane already carries `capacity` convoys.
rows.searched: fleet, vessel, ship pool, shipPool, vesselPool, fleetSize, flotilla, squadron, tonnage, hulls, berth, at sea, in port, put to sea, home port, 'already at sea', 'live operation'

rows.target: Cargo asymmetry (LG-3/LG-5; L-LG-4) — units flow toward the war and never back; return legs carry trade
rows.evidence: THE ONE-WAY OUTCOME IS ENFORCED, and the code says so in its own words. src/domain/worldPulse/navalKernel.js:304-317: 'CONVOY STAND-DOWN (design §2 — a convoy is a ONE-TIME crossing): on arrival the escort's work is done ⇒ retire the record and (if it escorts a live deployment) stamp that deployment DELIVERED, so the derive loop does not re-mint a shuttle for an army already at its target' — implemented at :316 `deliveryStamps[cargo] = { …dep, …, seaLiftDelivered: rec.targetId }` and re-checked at :338-340 (`const delivered = dep.seaLiftDelivered ?? deliveryStamps[armyId]?.seaLiftDelivered; if (delivered != null && String(delivered) === targetId) continue;`). A redirect to a NEW target re-derives; the same crossing never does. NO RETURN LEG OF ANY KIND. Greps for 'return leg', 'return voyage', 'return trip', backhaul, ballast, 'empty return' and 'sails back' find nothing maritime: the only live 'return leg' in the tree is src/domain/pendingEdits.js:52/:92, the V-24a RECALL RIDER that brings a TRAVELLING NPC home early over the roads mover. The retreat arm is overland/land-parity (navalLayer.js:7 'the loser retreats to home port' via `retreatRoute`), carries no cargo class, and there is no trade exemption — nothing anywhere types a return leg as carrying goods.

rows.target: News carriage (LG-8; §125.3 chain) — vessels carry origin news; a caravan-to-caravan chain
rows.evidence: THE VESSEL CARRIER IS BUILT AND FIRES. src/domain/spatial/rumorNetwork.js:80-85 declares it — 'the SHIP-CREW carrier lights WITH the sea lanes — a ship crew carries the news of its home port to the next port, FAST + LONG-RANGE (port-to-port news skips the land chain)' — and :745 actually dispatches it: `relayVia(RUMOR_CARRIER_SHIP, 'ship', shipNeighbours.get(sid) || [])`, inside `relayVia` (:690-740) which mints a real delivery packet with `arrivalTick: now + travelTicks` off the sea-aware `hopWeeks`. THE RELAY IS ALREADY A CHAIN, hop by hop: :682 `if (record.hopCount >= maxHopsFor(record)) continue;` then :683 `const hop = record.hopCount + 1`, with lineage and provenance appended per hop (:722-729) — so a telling walks town→town→town over trade edges (:744 `relayVia(RUMOR_CARRIER_TRADE,'merchant',tradeNeighbours(graph,sid))`, with :104-107 `RUMOR_TRADE_CHANNEL_TYPES` carrying news BOTH ways). WHAT IS MISSING: (a) NO AIRSHIP CARRIER — the closed carrier vocabulary is exactly six, at rumorNetwork.js:72/:73/:78/:85/:93/:101 (trade, army, criminal, ship, teleport, refugee), and no seventh exists anywhere; (b) the chain is SETTLEMENT-MEDIATED, never caravan-to-caravan — every relay hop originates at a settlement node `sid` and targets a `neighbourId`, so two caravans meeting on the road exchange nothing.
rows.searched: carries the news, carry the news, carries news, courier, messenger, caravan, carrier, news travels, word of, carried word, RUMOR_CARRIER, relayVia, shipNeighbours

rows.target: Envoy vessels (LG-7) — a named NPC travelling by ship / airship / circle
rows.evidence: THE SHIP ARM IS FULLY BUILT AND MODALITY-TYPED — a whole module the first pass's search missed. src/domain/roads/seaRoads.js:1-7: 'DEEP COUPLINGS D-6 THE SEA ROADS … Envoys, embassies, and captives travel by sea: a mission's route already folds sea edges when the digest is lit, so this slice adds MODALITY AWARENESS (per-hop land|sea), a sea-aware current-leg read, and a PASS-3 SEA-HAZARD branch'. It is not a docblock promise: `classifyLegModes(digest, path)` at :62-78 tags every hop 'land'|'sea' off the sea-edge adjacency; `currentSeaHop(m, weekClock, digest, season)` at :86-119 resolves which hop the traveller occupies and whether it is over water; `resolveSeaHazard(a)` at :148-201 dispatches S1 blockade capture (`{cls:'S1', outcome:'hostage', captorId, overSea:true}`), S2 seasonal storm delay and S3 piracy. AND IT IS WIRED: src/domain/worldPulse/roadsKernel.js:86 imports all four; :1032 freezes the modality at dispatch (`...(seaLit ? { legModes: classifyLegModes(digest, route.path) } : {})`); :610-611 dispatches the sea branch; and :622/:623/:642 suppress the LAND hazards on a sea hop (`!overSea`), so the modalities are genuinely exclusive. The travellers are envoys: roadsKernel.js:947/:967-983 assigns purposes embassy / diplomacy / dominion / verification off DIPLO_CATEGORY. It is dark behind the virtual flag `seaRoadsEnabled` (seaRoads.js:32-38), but the flag has a real reader and a lit test (tests/domain/seaRoadsLit.test.js:51). WHAT IS MISSING: the airship and circle arms. Grepping teleport/circle/airship across all of src/domain/roads/*.js and namedPersonTransit.js returns only two incidental lines (ops.js:92, state.js:167 — both the phrase 'never a teleport' meaning 'no instant jump'). `legModes` is a two-member vocabulary; there is no 'air' or 'circle' leg.
rows.searched: envoy, by ship, vessel, legModes, overSea, sea hop, modality, named NPC travel, teleport/circle/airship inside roads, arrives by, sea roads

rows.target: Confiscation + inspection split (LG-5; §125.2) — an army on the route takes or turns back a caravan; observed cargo × believed destination
rows.evidence: Seizure is a GATE act by a settlement, never an army act on the road, and there is no turn-back at all. src/domain/spatial/smuggle.js:250-261 is the whole disposition ladder — `if (detected && hostile) return 'seizure'; if (detected && contraband) return 'confiscation'; return 'toll';` — and :283 confirms the actor is a node: the read returns 'null when the route has no intermediary GATE at all'. Interception is likewise a gate predicate: src/domain/spatial/supplyShipments.js:198-209 `routeIntercepted(path, isHostileToDestination)` walks the path's intermediary SETTLEMENTS. Greps for requisition, commandeer, impound and 'search the cargo' return ZERO hits anywhere in src/ or supabase/; 'turn back' hits only migration prose (src/domain/worldPulse/demographicsMigration.js:476 'A column that could not land turns back', about arrivals) and roadsKernel.js:480 (a traveller turning homeward). The two registers of the §125.2 split exist but never multiply: the OBSERVED-CARGO register is smuggle.js's `contraband` flag (:269 'the cargo is contraband here'), evaluated at ARRIVAL at a gate; the BELIEVED-DESTINATION register is src/domain/spatial/dispatchEV.js:185 'THE DETERRENT — believed destination danger (reads BELIEF, never truth)', evaluated at DISPATCH by the sender. Different actor, different moment, no product term. The one army-on-route hook that exists is roadsKernel.js:623 `armyOnHop(...)` — and it captures a NAMED PERSON, not a cargo.

rows.target: Siege lockdown + capture by captor relation (LG-9..12) — exits by smuggler/tunnel/circle; friendly release, enemy ransom
rows.evidence: BOTH HALVES HAVE REAL, WIRED CODE — under names the first pass did not search. (1) SIEGE LOCKDOWN: src/domain/worldPulse/roadsKernel.js:638 `res = fork.random() < p ? {cls:'T2', outcome:'hostage', captorId} : {cls:'T2', outcome:'trapped', captorId};` — a traveller at a besieged destination is taken or TRAPPED; :736-739 latches it (`m.trappedBySiege = true`) with a news beat; :317 `if (m.trappedBySiege) return null;` blanks the expected-return week; and :489-490 releases on the siege lifting — 'A lifted siege releases a trapped guest (§7 T2 extension)' / `if (m.trappedBySiege && !warFrontsInto(graph, str(m.destId)).length) m.trappedBySiege = false;`. The typed field is declared at src/domain/roads/state.js:85/:119. (2) CAPTOR RELATION: roadsKernel.js:676 stamps it at capture — `const hostileAtCapture = atOpenWar(graph, homeId, res.captorId) || HOSTILE_RUNGS.has(relationshipTypeBetween(graph, worldState, homeId, res.captorId));` — persisted on the ransom record at :685, and :783 spends it: `else if (r.hostileAtCapture && !atOpenWar(graph, homeId, captorId) && !HOSTILE_RUNGS.has(relationshipTypeBetween(...))) early = 'peace';`, with :820 confirming 'every other early release (rescue, captor_gone, occupied, peace) skips all credits' — i.e. amnesty pays no ransom, while a term run to its end at :823-826 bills the full schedule. src/domain/roads/state.js:105-106 documents it: 'hostile-then-peaceful ⇒ amnesty'. WHAT IS MISSING: the EXIT-MODE SET. The trap is absolute — there is no smuggler, tunnel or circle exit for a trapped traveller. Greps for lockdown, postern, 'slip out', 'smuggled out' return zero; the two 'underways' couplings are goods and the dead, not living exits under siege (src/domain/worldPulse/foodStockpile.js:317-321 'a tunneled town keeps a bounded supply trickle under siege'; src/domain/worldPulse/settlementLifecycleFirstClass.js:605-609 'Escaped through the underways: fate unresolved' — a dispersal RECEIPT on settlement death, explicitly 'a receipt only, never a fate').

rows.target: Roaming captivity without ransom (§125.5) — a bounded hold with no ransom; the bandit producer maybe owed
rows.evidence: Every captivity in the tree is anchored to a SETTLEMENT captor, which is exactly what §125.5 excludes. In the roads mover the captor is always an id in the world roster: roadsKernel.js:775 `else if (!idSet.has(captorId)) early = 'captor_gone';` — a captor that is not a settlement ends the captivity rather than sustaining it — and the T3 banditry arm mints the same shape with a settlement id (roadsKernel.js:602-603/:649-650 `captorId` = the embattled NODE, and the sea twin at seaRoads.js:194 `const captorId = a.idSet.has(port) ? port : a.destId;`). The ransom mint hard-requires a settlement debtor: src/domain/worldPulse/ransomClaim.js:170-186 — 'The debtor is the person's OWN home … the realm that sent him is the only party who can pay it' — `const debtorId = strictText(homeId); if (!debtorId || !worth) return {claim:null, reason:'invalid_demand'};` plus :186 `if (debtorId === captorId) return {claim:null, reason:'captor_is_home'};`. I DID find the nearest fragment and it refutes rather than supports: src/domain/worldPulse/foreignGuestHold.js:36-42 and :53-58 give a custody ledger with causes including `private_imprisonment` and close reasons `release/escape/death/pardon` — a bounded hold that CAN close with no ransom minted — but its `captorId` (:72/:316/:331) and `venueId` are settlement-side ids fed by src/domain/worldPulse/envoyInterceptionStage.js:404, so this is the adjacent landed settlement-custody family the §125.5 row was distinguished FROM, not a fragment of it. Nothing owes a bandit producer anything: 'bandit' appears only as a label (roadsKernel.js:588-589 'a bandit road (T3) can still take an embassy … bandits do not parley').

rows.target: Size-scaled speed (§125.4, WY/POP-adjacent) — armies and columns move slower the larger they are
rows.evidence: Neither mover reads size. The army speed function takes exactly two inputs and neither is a headcount: src/domain/spatial/armyTransit.js:294-301 `export function armyMarchWeeks(baseHopWeeks, readiness01 = 0.5) { … const speedMult = 1 + T.READINESS_SPEED_GAIN * (rdy - 0.5) * 2; const weeks = Math.ceil((base * T.ARMY_SPEED_FACTOR) / Math.max(0.1, speedMult)); … }` — a flat `ARMY_SPEED_FACTOR: 1.5` (:56) modulated only by readiness (`READINESS_SPEED_GAIN: 0.4`, :57). The tuning comment at :53-55 names the very reason size WOULD matter and then does not use it: 'An army marches SLOWER than a courier/caravan: baggage, foraging, formation.' Strength is used elsewhere in the same file (fatigue, battle, attrition) but never in the speed term. The migration column is worse — pure hop time with no column term at all: src/domain/worldPulse/migrationKernel.js:223 `const weeks = hopWeeks(digest, originId, destId, season);` → :262 `arrivalTick: tick + weeks`. The only 'size-scaled' phrase in the mover is about crime, not speed (migrationKernel.js:74 'size-scaled crime (§II.3-3)'). The naval twin is a per-mode constant too (navalLayer.js:78 'A laden convoy is a little slower than an empty courier').

rows.target: Declared widening of saved data (Q7 / L-LG-2 / Q5) — a commitments ledger plus circle/dock as persisted settlement features
rows.evidence: The persisted-shape widening was never taken, and the code has deliberately chosen the opposite policy.
